102	    // MARK: - Finding the user's ffmpeg
103	
104	    /// A located install. `ffprobe` is required, not optional: without it the
105	    /// codecs inside the container are unknown, and the honest choice would
106	    /// then be to assume the worst and re-encode a file that only needed
107	    /// repackaging. Spending an hour of somebody's CPU on a guess is worse
108	    /// than the status quo, so a half install degrades to no install. Every
109	    /// ffmpeg distribution for macOS — Homebrew, MacPorts, the static
110	    /// builds — ships both binaries together.
111	    struct Tools {
112	        let ffmpeg: URL
113	        let ffprobe: URL
114	    }
115	
116	    /// Where to look, in order, when `RCFFmpegPath` is unset. `PATH` comes
117	    /// first because a user who put a build ahead of Homebrew's meant it;
118	    /// the literal list follows because a GUI app launched from the Finder
119	    /// inherits `launchd`'s `PATH` (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`), which
120	    /// contains no ffmpeg on any Mac. `/opt/homebrew` is spec §11's own
121	    /// example and is first among the literals on Apple silicon; the rest
122	    /// cover Intel Homebrew, MacPorts and a hand-installed binary.
123	    private static let searchDirectories = [
124	        "/opt/homebrew/bin", "/usr/local/bin", "/opt/local/bin", "/usr/bin", "/bin",
125	    ]
126	
127	    /// The located tools, or `nil` when the user has no usable ffmpeg — the
128	    /// answer that makes every caller fall back to exactly today's behaviour.
129	    ///
130	    /// Cached for the life of the process: this is a handful of `stat` calls
131	    /// and an import funnel would otherwise repeat them per file, but the
132	    /// point is really that the answer must not change halfway through a
133	    /// batch drop.
134	    static func tools() -> Tools? {
135	        stateLock.lock()
136	        defer { stateLock.unlock() }
137	        if let resolved = resolvedTools { return resolved.value }
138	        let found = locate()
139	        resolvedTools = Box(found)
140	        return found
141	    }
142	
143	    private static func locate() -> Tools? {
144	        guard let ffmpeg = locate("ffmpeg") else { return nil }
145	        // ffprobe sits next to ffmpeg in every install; prefer that sibling
146	        // over a `PATH` search so a user pointing `RCFFmpegPath` at one build
147	        // does not silently get another build's probe.
148	        let sibling = ffmpeg.deletingLastPathComponent().appendingPathComponent("ffprobe")
149	        if isExecutable(sibling) { return Tools(ffmpeg: ffmpeg, ffprobe: sibling) }
150	        guard let ffprobe = locate("ffprobe") else { return nil }
151	        return Tools(ffmpeg: ffmpeg, ffprobe: ffprobe)
152	    }
153	
154	    private static func locate(_ name: String) -> URL? {
155	        if name == "ffmpeg", let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: toolDefaultsKey) {
156	            let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)
157	            return isExecutable(url) ? url : nil
158	        }
159	        let path = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["PATH"] ?? ""
160	        let directories = path.split(separator: ":").map(String.init) + searchDirectories
161	        for directory in directories where !directory.isEmpty {
162	            let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: directory, isDirectory: true)
163	                .appendingPathComponent(name)
164	            if isExecutable(url) { return url }
165	        }
166	        return nil
167	    }
168	
169	    private static func isExecutable(_ url: URL) -> Bool {
170	        var isDirectory: ObjCBool = false
171	        let manager = FileManager.default
172	        guard manager.fileExists(atPath: url.path, isDirectory: &isDirectory),
173	            !isDirectory.boolValue
174	        else { return false }
175	        return manager.isExecutableFile(atPath: url.path)
176	    }

178	    // MARK: - Where the converted file goes
179	
180	    /// `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`.
181	    ///
182	    /// **Why not inside the `.framejob` package**, which is what spec §11's
183	    /// one-line sketch says. Two reasons, both discovered in the code:
184	    ///
185	    /// 1. There is frequently no package. Opening an MKV from the Finder
186	    ///    builds an UNTITLED document (`ProjectDocument.readMediaFile` nils
187	    ///    `fileURL` deliberately, and `intendedCacheDirectory` falls back to a
188	    ///    temporary directory precisely because of it). The import that needs
189	    ///    the conversion is the very import that has nowhere to put it, and a
190	    ///    file written to `NSTemporaryDirectory()` is orphaned by the first
191	    ///    Save As — which costs nothing for a regenerable thumbnail and loses
192	    ///    the user's footage here.
193	    /// 2. `ProjectDocument.fileWrapper(ofType:)` writes a package with
194	    ///    exactly two children, `project.json` and `cache`. Anything else put
195	    ///    in the bundle is dropped by the next save, autosave included. The
196	    ///    one surviving location, `cache/`, is documented as regenerable and
197	    ///    deletable (§5.6) — the last place to keep the only decodable copy of
198	    ///    somebody's source material.
199	    ///
200	    /// Application Support has neither problem: it exists before the document
201	    /// does, it survives every save and Save As, and a reopened project finds
202	    /// the file by the same absolute path it recorded. It is also shared, so
203	    /// importing the same MKV into a second project reuses the first
204	    /// conversion instead of paying for it twice. This keeps the §11 decision
205	    /// intact — media is *referenced*, not copied into the document — and the
206	    /// converted file behaves like any other referenced media: move it and the
207	    /// Media tab badges it missing and offers Relink…
208	    ///
209	    /// The two path components were spelled here, privately, until road map
210	    /// 2's phase 7 needed the same folder for `ExportPresets.json`. They are
211	    /// `AppSupport`'s now — one home for `~/Library/Application
212	    /// Support/Frame Job/`, which is where the argument above still lives; this
213	    /// only names the subfolder. The directory itself is still created by
214	    /// `convert`, at the moment there is something to put in it.
215	    static var rewrapDirectory: URL? {
216	        AppSupport.subdirectory("Rewrapped")
217	    }
218	
219	    /// The converted file's name for `source`: the source's own stem, so the
220	    /// Media tab still reads recognisably, plus a digest of the source's
221	    /// path, size and modification date. The digest is what makes the result
222	    /// reusable AND self-invalidating — re-importing the same file finds the
223	    /// existing conversion, while re-encoding the source under the same name
224	    /// produces a different digest and a fresh conversion rather than a stale
225	    /// one.
226	    static func destination(for source: URL) -> URL? {
227	        guard let directory = rewrapDirectory, let digest = digest(of: source) else { return nil }
228	        return directory.appendingPathComponent("\(stem(of: source))-\(digest).mov")
229	    }
230	
231	    /// A finished conversion of `source`, if one is already on disk. Checked
232	    /// before ffmpeg is even looked for, so a project whose media was
233	    /// converted last month still opens on a machine where ffmpeg has since
234	    /// been uninstalled.
235	    static func existingRewrap(of source: URL) -> URL? {
236	        guard let destination = destination(for: source),
237	            FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: destination.path)
238	        else { return nil }
239	        return destination
240	    }
241	
242	    /// Throws away a conversion that turned out to be unopenable, so the next
243	    /// import tries again instead of handing the same bad file back for ever
244	    /// — `existingRewrap` cannot tell a good `.mov` from a bad one, and only
245	    /// the caller that re-probed it knows.
246	    ///
247	    /// Refuses to delete anything that is not directly inside
248	    /// `rewrapDirectory`. This takes a URL and removes a file, which is
249	    /// exactly the shape of function that a bug elsewhere turns into a data
250	    /// loss, so the guard is not a formality.
251	    static func discard(_ url: URL) {
252	        guard let directory = rewrapDirectory,
253	            url.deletingLastPathComponent().standardizedFileURL.path
254	                == directory.standardizedFileURL.path
255	        else { return }
256	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
257	    }
258	
259	    /// FNV-1a over path, byte size and modification second. Not a content
260	    /// hash: reading gigabytes to decide whether to convert gigabytes is the
261	    /// wrong trade, and the three attributes together already distinguish
262	    /// every file this will ever see. A collision would reuse the wrong
263	    /// conversion, which is why the *name* also carries the source's stem.
264	    private static func digest(of source: URL) -> String? {
265	        let attributes = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: source.path)
266	        guard let size = (attributes?[.size] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value else { return nil }
267	        let modified = (attributes?[.modificationDate] as? Date)?.timeIntervalSince1970 ?? 0
268	        var hash: UInt64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325
269	        for byte in "\(source.path)|\(size)|\(Int64(modified.rounded()))".utf8 {
270	            hash = (hash ^ UInt64(byte)) &* 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3
271	        }
272	        let hex = String(hash, radix: 16)
273	        return String(repeating: "0", count: max(0, 16 - hex.count)) + hex
274	    }
275	
276	    /// The source's base name reduced to characters that are unambiguous in a
277	    /// file name. This string is built from a file name the app did not
278	    /// choose, and it becomes a path component — so it is filtered rather
279	    /// than trusted, and bounded so a pathological name cannot push the
280	    /// result past the file system's limit.
281	    private static func stem(of source: URL) -> String {
282	        let allowed = CharacterSet.alphanumerics.union(CharacterSet(charactersIn: "-_"))
283	        let characters = source.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent.unicodeScalars.map {
284	            allowed.contains($0) ? Character($0) : "_"
285	        }
286	        let text = String(characters.prefix(48))
287	        return text.isEmpty ? "media" : text
288	    }

290	    // MARK: - Consent
291	
292	    /// Puts the cost in front of the user and returns their answer. Safe from
293	    /// any thread; on a background thread it hops to main and waits, which is
294	    /// sound because `assist` deliberately holds no lock across this call —
295	    /// see the comment there.
296	    static func consent(for plan: Plan) -> Bool {
297	        if Thread.isMainThread { return ask(plan) }
298	        var accepted = false
299	        DispatchQueue.main.sync { accepted = ask(plan) }
300	        return accepted
301	    }
302	
303	    private static func ask(_ plan: Plan) -> Bool {
304	        let alert = NSAlert()
305	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
306	        alert.messageText = "Frame Job cannot open “\(plan.source.lastPathComponent)”."
307	        alert.informativeText = plan.consentText
308	        alert.addButton(withTitle: plan.isStreamCopy ? "Repackage" : "Convert")
309	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
310	        alert.showsSuppressionButton = true
311	        alert.suppressionButton?.title = "Do this automatically from now on"
312	        let accepted = alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn
313	        // "From now on" means the answer just given, not always yes: a user
314	        // who cancels with the box ticked is asking never to see this again.
315	        if alert.suppressionButton?.state == .on { remember(accepted ? .always : .never) }
316	        return accepted
317	    }

319	    // MARK: - Orchestration
320	
321	    /// The whole opt-in step: a file AVFoundation refused goes in, a file it
322	    /// can open comes out.
323	    ///
324	    /// * `nil` — no help is available or none was wanted (no ffmpeg, the
325	    ///   policy says no, the user cancelled, ffprobe found nothing to
326	    ///   import). The caller reports AVFoundation's own failure, which is
327	    ///   exactly the behaviour of a machine with no ffmpeg on it.
328	    /// * a URL — a movie on disk under the `.mov` digest name (MP4-format
329	    ///   for a VP9 copy), ready to probe.
330	    /// * a throw — the conversion was authorised and failed, which is worth
331	    ///   its own message rather than "could not read".
332	    ///
333	    /// Synchronous and long by design (`longestAssist` is its bound): it is
334	    /// called from `MediaImporter`'s two synchronous faces, OUTSIDE the
335	    /// 30-second ceiling those put on the AVFoundation probe, because a
336	    /// transcode legitimately takes minutes and being killed at 30 seconds
337	    /// would be a bug rather than a safeguard. `mayAsk` is the CALLER's (spec
338	    /// §11 MC-5): false for a tool call's import, where nobody is at the
339	    /// keyboard, so there the stored policy decides alone and `ask` means no.
340	    ///
341	    /// `reencodingVP9` is the second attempt after a VP9 copy failed, failed
342	    /// its frame check or would not open (spec §11 #227): it answers `nil`
343	    /// for a source whose plan is not a VP9 copy before any question, and
344	    /// re-encodes the video, once per file: a re-encode this process made
345	    /// and kept is answered instead of discarded. `planned` is the first
346	    /// attempt's plan, set before its question, which the second attempt
347	    /// takes instead of running ffprobe again.
348	    static func assist(
349	        _ source: URL, mayAsk: Bool, planned: inout Plan?, reencodingVP9: Bool = false
350	    ) throws -> URL? {
351	        // Before ffmpeg is even looked for, and before the policy is even
352	        // read: a conversion already on disk is already paid for. The policy
353	        // governs whether ffmpeg RUNS, and reusing a finished file runs
354	        // nothing — a user who turned the feature off to stop being asked
355	        // should still get the copy they made last week.
356	        if !reencodingVP9, let existing = existingRewrap(of: source) { return existing }
357	
358	        // Read once, and read BEFORE ffprobe is spawned: a user who said
359	        // never, and a tool call's import with nobody to ask, should cost
360	        // nothing beyond the `stat` above.
361	        let decided = policy
362	        if decided == .never || (decided == .ask && !mayAsk) { return nil }
363	        guard let tools = tools(),
364	            var plan = (reencodingVP9 ? planned : nil) ?? plan(for: source, with: tools)
365	        else { return nil }
366	        if reencodingVP9 {
367	            guard plan.copiesVP9 else { return nil }
368	            plan = plan.reencodingVideo()
369	        } else {
370	            planned = plan
371	        }
372	        if decided == .ask, !consent(for: plan) { return nil }
373	
374	        // The lock starts HERE and not above. Consent can block on the main
375	        // thread, and the main thread can itself be inside this function
376	        // (`ProjectDocument.read(from:ofType:)` is allowed to run there) — so
377	        // a lock held across the alert would be a background thread waiting
378	        // for main while main waits for the lock. Two imports of the same
379	        // file may therefore both ask; the second finds the finished file on
380	        // the re-check below and never runs ffmpeg twice.
381	        conversionLock.lock()
382	        defer { conversionLock.unlock() }
383	        if reencodingVP9 {
384	            // Another import of this file may have re-encoded it while this
385	            // one waited: that file is kept, not discarded (spec §11 #227).
386	            if isKeptReencode(plan.destination) { return plan.destination }
387	            discard(plan.destination)
388	        } else if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: plan.destination.path) {
389	            return plan.destination
390	        }
391	        let made = try convert(plan, with: tools)
392	        if reencodingVP9 { noteReencode(made) }
393	        return made
394	    }

396	    // MARK: - Running ffmpeg
397	
398	    private static func convert(_ plan: Plan, with tools: Tools) throws -> URL {
399	        let manager = FileManager.default
400	        guard (try? AppSupport.ensureDirectory(plan.destination.deletingLastPathComponent()))
401	            != nil
402	        else {
403	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, "the conversion folder could not be created")
404	        }
405	
406	        // Written under a partial name and moved into place, so a crash, a
407	        // kill or a full disk leaves no truncated file that `existingRewrap`
408	        // would later hand out as finished.
409	        let partial = plan.destination.deletingPathExtension()
410	            .appendingPathExtension("partial.mov")
411	        try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
412	
413	        let result: ToolResult
414	        do {
415	            result = try run(
416	                tools.ffmpeg, arguments(for: plan, with: tools, writing: partial),
417	                timeout: timeout(for: plan))
418	        } catch let failure as ToolFailure {
419	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
420	            throw failure.timedOut
421	                ? RewrapError.timedOut(plan.source)
422	                : RewrapError.failed(plan.source, failure.detail)
423	        }
424	        guard result.status == 0, manager.fileExists(atPath: partial.path) else {
425	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
426	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, lastLine(of: result.errorOutput))
427	        }
428	        // A VP9 copy is kept only when every frame is on its rate's grid
429	        // (spec §11 #227), checked here so no unchecked copy ever holds the
430	        // name `existingRewrap` hands out.
431	        let exact = !plan.copiesVP9 || keepsFrameGrid(partial, of: plan, with: tools)
432	        guard exact else {
433	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
434	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, "")
435	        }
436	        do {
437	            try manager.moveItem(at: partial, to: plan.destination)
438	        } catch {
439	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
440	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, error.localizedDescription)
441	        }
442	        return plan.destination
443	    }

445	    /// Asked once per process, and only on the transcode path — a stream copy
446	    /// never needs an encoder, and spawning a process to find that out would
447	    /// tax the common case for nothing. Takes `tools` rather than calling
448	    /// `tools()`: this runs inside `convert`, and the two functions must not
449	    /// contend for the same lock (`stateLock` here, `conversionLock` there).
450	    static func hasLibX264(_ tools: Tools) -> Bool {
451	        stateLock.lock()
452	        defer { stateLock.unlock() }
453	        if let known = libX264 { return known }
454	        let result = try? run(
455	            tools.ffmpeg, ["-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-encoders"],
456	            timeout: encoderQueryTimeout)
457	        let text = String(decoding: result?.output ?? Data(), as: UTF8.self)
458	        let found = text.split(separator: "\n").contains { line in
459	            line.split(separator: " ").contains("libx264")
460	        }
461	        libX264 = found
462	        return found
463	    }
464	
465	    /// How long ffmpeg gets. Generous, because the user consented to the
466	    /// cost and a slow disk is not a failure — but bounded, because a hung
467	    /// ffmpeg would otherwise hold the import path for ever. A copy is I/O
468	    /// and finishes in about the time it takes to read the file; an encode
469	    /// runs at some multiple of real time.
470	    private static func timeout(for plan: Plan) -> TimeInterval {
471	        let duration = max(0, plan.duration)
472	        let ceiling = plan.isStreamCopy ? max(300, duration * 2) : max(1800, duration * 30)
473	        return min(ceiling, longestConversion)
474	    }
475	
476	    /// The longest ffmpeg is ever given; `import_media`'s wait covers two
477	    /// (`longestAssist`).
478	    static let longestConversion: TimeInterval = 4 * 3600
479	
480	    private static func lastLine(of data: Data) -> String {
481	        let text = String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
482	        let lines = text.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).map {
483	            $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
484	        }
485	        return lines.last(where: { !$0.isEmpty }) ?? ""
486	    }

488	    // MARK: - Process plumbing
489	
490	    struct ToolResult {
491	        let status: Int32
492	        let output: Data
493	        let errorOutput: Data
494	    }
495	
496	    /// Runs one tool with an argument ARRAY and no shell between here and it,
497	    /// which is the only reason a file named with a semicolon or a backtick
498	    /// is harmless.
499	    ///
500	    /// Both pipes are drained on their own queues while the process runs:
501	    /// reading them after `waitUntilExit` deadlocks the moment ffmpeg writes
502	    /// more than a pipe buffer's worth of diagnostics, which a long encode
503	    /// certainly does.
504	    static func run(_ tool: URL, _ arguments: [String], timeout: TimeInterval) throws
505	        -> ToolResult {
506	        let process = Process()
507	        process.executableURL = tool
508	        process.arguments = arguments
509	        // No terminal, and nothing for a tool to read: a child that blocks on
510	        // stdin would otherwise hang until the timeout.
511	        process.standardInput = FileHandle.nullDevice
512	        let outPipe = Pipe()
513	        let errPipe = Pipe()
514	        process.standardOutput = outPipe
515	        process.standardError = errPipe
516	
517	        let collected = OutputBox()
518	        let drained = DispatchGroup()
519	        let exited = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
520	        process.terminationHandler = { _ in exited.signal() }
521	
522	        do {
523	            try process.run()
524	        } catch {
525	            throw ToolFailure(detail: error.localizedDescription, timedOut: false)
526	        }
527	        for (pipe, isError) in [(outPipe, false), (errPipe, true)] {
528	            drained.enter()
529	            DispatchQueue.global(qos: .utility).async {
530	                collected.append(pipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile(), isError: isError)
531	                drained.leave()
532	            }
533	        }
534	
535	        if exited.wait(timeout: .now() + timeout) != .success {
536	            process.terminate()
537	            if exited.wait(timeout: .now() + runGrace / 2) != .success, process.isRunning {
538	                kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)
539	            }
540	            _ = drained.wait(timeout: .now() + runGrace / 2)
541	            throw ToolFailure(
542	                detail: "\(tool.lastPathComponent) did not finish in time", timedOut: true)
543	        }
544	        process.waitUntilExit()
545	        _ = drained.wait(timeout: .now() + runGrace / 2)
546	        return ToolResult(
547	            status: process.terminationStatus, output: collected.output,
548	            errorOutput: collected.errorOutput)
549	    }

551	    /// Two background readers write into one of these; the caller reads it
552	    /// only after both have finished, and the lock covers the overlap.
553	    private final class OutputBox {
554	        private let boxLock = NSLock()
555	        private var out = Data()
556	        private var err = Data()
557	
558	        func append(_ data: Data, isError: Bool) {
559	            boxLock.lock()
560	            defer { boxLock.unlock() }
561	            if isError { err.append(data) } else { out.append(data) }
562	        }
563	
564	        var output: Data {
565	            boxLock.lock()
566	            defer { boxLock.unlock() }
567	            return out
568	        }
569	
570	        var errorOutput: Data {
571	            boxLock.lock()
572	            defer { boxLock.unlock() }
573	            return err
574	        }
575	    }
576	
577	    /// A once-computed answer that is allowed to be "no" — `Optional` alone
578	    /// could not tell "not looked yet" from "looked, found nothing".
579	    private final class Box {
580	        let value: Tools?
581	        init(_ value: Tools?) { self.value = value }
582	    }
583	
584	    /// Guards the two once-computed answers below. Held only across a `stat`
585	    /// sweep or one short `-encoders` call, never across a conversion.
586	    private static let stateLock = NSLock()
587	    private static var resolvedTools: Box?
588	    private static var libX264: Bool?
589	
590	    /// Serialises the conversions themselves, so two imports of one file
591	    /// cannot write the same destination at the same time. Deliberately a
592	    /// SECOND lock: `assist` holds this one for the length of an ffmpeg run,
593	    /// and `hasLibX264` runs inside that — one lock for both would deadlock
594	    /// on the first transcode.
595	    private static let conversionLock = NSLock()
596	}

7	/// Everything that reads a media FILE: probing it into the `media[]`
8	/// descriptor `add_media` takes, and generating the two caches the timeline
9	/// draws from (spec §7.7).
10	///
11	/// This is the ONE file where `async`/`await` is allowed (app/CLAUDE.md):
12	/// AVFoundation's property loading is async-only going forward, and the
13	/// alternative — the deprecated synchronous accessors — blocks the main
14	/// thread on a network volume. Callers outside this file stay synchronous by
15	/// using the completion-handler wrappers (`probe(url:completion:)`,
16	/// `generateCaches(for:url:in:)`), which keep every `await` on this side of
17	/// the seam.
18	///
19	/// The other half of the media story lives in `MediaDescriptor.swift`:
20	/// `MediaDescriptor` (what `probe` returns) and `mediaURL(for:)` /
21	/// `bookmarkString(for:)` (how a descriptor's path is resolved back to a
22	/// file).
23	enum MediaImporter {
24	
25	    // MARK: - Probing
26	
27	    /// The `media[]` descriptor for a file: duration, display size, rate and
28	    /// the two track flags (spec §7.7). Throws `ImportError` for a file
29	    /// nothing can open; never crashes on a truncated or hostile file.
30	    ///
31	    /// The size reported is the DISPLAY size — `naturalSize` through
32	    /// `preferredTransform` — so a portrait iPhone clip imports as
33	    /// 1080×1920, not 1920×1080 with a rotation nobody applied. Getting this
34	    /// wrong is invisible until the first phone clip lands sideways on the
35	    /// canvas, which is why it is the verification of M1 step 3.
36	    ///
37	    /// **AVFoundation only.** The opt-in ffmpeg step lives one level up, in
38	    /// `probeAllowingRewrap`, so this stays the pure "what does the system
39	    /// think of this file" question that the rewrap's own re-probe can ask
40	    /// without recursing.
41	    static func probe(url: URL) async throws -> MediaDescriptor {
42	        if isLUT(url) { return try probeLUT(url) }
43	        if isImage(url) { return try probeImage(url) }
44	        return try await probeAsset(url)
45	    }
46	
47	    /// One AVFoundation probe, waited for from whatever thread called —
48	    /// `probeBlocking`'s original body, now shared with the
49	    /// completion-handler face and used twice per assisted import (once on
50	    /// the file the user chose, once on what ffmpeg made of it).
51	    static func waitForProbe(_ url: URL) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
52	        let box = ProbeBox()
53	        let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
54	        Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
55	            do {
56	                box.outcome = .success(try await probe(url: url))
57	            } catch {
58	                box.outcome = .failure(error)
59	            }
60	            semaphore.signal()
61	        }
62	        // Generous, and only a backstop: a probe reads headers and decodes one frame.
63	        // A file on a stalled network mount is the case this exists for.
64	        guard semaphore.wait(timeout: .now() + probeTimeout) == .success,
65	            let outcome = box.outcome
66	        else {
67	            throw ImportError.timedOut(url)
68	        }
69	        return try outcome.get()
70	    }
71	
72	    /// AVFoundation's view of a movie or a sound file.
73	    private static func probeAsset(_ url: URL) async throws -> MediaDescriptor {
74	        let asset = AVURLAsset(url: url, options: [AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey: true])
75	        guard let duration = try? await asset.load(.duration), duration.isNumeric else {
76	            throw ImportError.unreadable(url)
77	        }
78	        let videoTracks = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .video)) ?? []
79	        let audioTracks = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio)) ?? []
80	        guard !videoTracks.isEmpty || !audioTracks.isEmpty else {
81	            throw ImportError.noTracks(url)
82	        }
83	
84	        var width = 0
85	        var height = 0
86	        var fps = Fps.thirty
87	        var hasAlpha = false
88	        var color: MediaColor?
89	        if let track = videoTracks.first {
90	            let natural = (try? await track.load(.naturalSize)) ?? .zero
91	            let transform = (try? await track.load(.preferredTransform)) ?? .identity
92	            // `applying` maps the whole rectangle, so a 90° preferred
93	            // transform swaps the components and negates one of them; the
94	            // magnitudes are the display size.
95	            let mapped = natural.applying(transform)
96	            width = Int(abs(mapped.width).rounded())
97	            height = Int(abs(mapped.height).rounded())
98	            fps = await frameRate(of: track)
99	            let descriptions = (try? await track.load(.formatDescriptions)) ?? []
100	            hasAlpha = hasAlphaChannel(descriptions)
101	            color = detectedColor(descriptions) ?? detectedPQ(descriptions, track: track, asset: asset)
102	            // One frame through the decoder: `isPlayable` says yes to files
103	            // nothing here decodes (spec §11 #216).
104	            guard DecoderSupport.decodesFirstFrame(of: track, in: asset) else {
105	                throw ImportError.undecodable(url, sentence: DecoderSupport.refusal(
106	                    fileName: url.lastPathComponent, descriptions: descriptions))
107	            }
108	        }
109	
110	        let kind: MediaKind = videoTracks.isEmpty ? .audio : .video
111	        return MediaDescriptor(
112	            path: url.path, bookmark: bookmarkString(for: url), kind: kind,
113	            duration: CompositionBuilder.ticks(duration), width: width, height: height, fps: fps,
114	            hasVideo: !videoTracks.isEmpty, hasAudio: !audioTracks.isEmpty, hasAlpha: hasAlpha,
115	            color: color)
116	    }
117	
118	    /// A track's rate as an exact rational. `nominalFrameRate` is a Float and
119	    /// lies slightly (29.97003 for 30000/1001), so it is matched against the
120	    /// common rates rather than trusted; a file that reports nothing falls
121	    /// back to `minFrameDuration`, which IS exact when the container carries
122	    /// it.
123	    private static func frameRate(of track: AVAssetTrack) async -> Fps {
124	        var nominal = Double((try? await track.load(.nominalFrameRate)) ?? 0)
125	        if !(nominal > 0), let minimum = try? await track.load(.minFrameDuration),
126	            minimum.isNumeric, minimum.seconds > 0 {
127	            nominal = 1 / minimum.seconds
128	        }
129	        return rationalFrameRate(nominal)
130	    }

132	    // MARK: - Cache generation
133	
134	    /// Kicks off both caches in the background and returns immediately —
135	    /// the synchronous entry point every call site uses: the open path, the
136	    /// import path, the three relink paths, Consolidate and Add Background,
137	    /// all through `ProjectDocument.generateCaches`'s whole-media loop. That
138	    /// loop is cheap to run over media whose caches are done: the task stats
139	    /// the file ONCE into a `CacheStamp` (`MediaCacheFiles.swift`) and hands
140	    /// it to both halves, each of which reads its completion marker and
141	    /// returns when the two are equal — one stat, a marker read per half and
142	    /// a `fileExists` for the `.bin` per media with nothing to do, and a
143	    /// decode only for one whose file is new, changed, or whose last pass
144	    /// never finished. One stamp for both halves is also what keeps the two
145	    /// markers from disagreeing when the file changes between them. A nil
146	    /// stamp (the file cannot be stat'ed) is enqueued and runs like any
147	    /// other: it can neither skip nor mark, and running is the conservative
148	    /// direction — the cache is made, and nothing certifies it.
149	    ///
150	    /// Nothing cancels the task but a pass asked for another file (below) —
151	    /// not the document closing, not a save — and since a marker is written
152	    /// after the last frame and never before, a pass cut short leaves a
153	    /// strip with no marker for the next call to rebuild. A FIRST SAVE while
154	    /// a pass runs: the task keeps writing into the temporary directory it
155	    /// captured while `fileWrapper(ofType:)` copies into the package only
156	    /// what had landed, and nothing re-runs the pass after a save. Process
157	    /// death. And a save of a TITLED document, which lists the package for
158	    /// its lazy `cache/` wrapper and SWAPS the new package in: no marker,
159	    /// waveform or voice file is written between the save's `saveBegan` and
160	    /// `saveEnded` (`ProjectDocument+CacheSaves.swift`,
161	    /// `CacheLedger.publish`), so each lands by path in the package the save
162	    /// swapped in. A frame is not held, so one written in that window goes
163	    /// with the old package, and `thumbnails` then writes no marker
164	    /// (`stripHolds`, inside the same `publish`).
165	    ///
166	    /// One CURRENT pass per (cache directory, media id): a superseded pass may
167	    /// still be finishing beside it, writing nothing more. Two passes for
168	    /// one media can be asked for in quick succession — open then relink,
169	    /// relink twice, import then Consolidate — and frames from two SOURCES
170	    /// interleaving in one `thumbs/<id>/` would be certified by the later
171	    /// marker. So a pass for the SAME file awaits the one asked for before
172	    /// it, in call order, and because each pass re-checks the marker at its
173	    /// head, a queued redundant pass costs the no-op price above. A pass for
174	    /// ANOTHER file supersedes: the ledger cancels the running task, the new
175	    /// pass waits for it at most `CacheLedger.waitLimit` (`awaitPass`), and
176	    /// the superseded pass writes nothing more, since every frame, head
177	    /// clear and publication asks `pass.isCurrent()` first. So a pass stuck
178	    /// on a stalled volume no longer holds a relink away from it. The
179	    /// bookkeeping is `CacheLedger` (`MediaCacheLedger.swift`, where nothing
180	    /// awaits); the awaiting is here, inside the task, so this stays
181	    /// synchronous.
182	    ///
183	    /// A waveform or loudness pass that published nothing is retried in the
184	    /// same task after each of `peaksRetryDelays` while the pass is current
185	    /// (`retryPeaks`), so a lost waveform does not wait for the next open.
186	    /// Its four audio decodes run on the cache lane (`onCacheLane`, spec §11 #367).
187	    static func generateCaches(
188	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL, urls: [UInt32: URL] = [:]
189	    ) {
190	        guard media.kind != .lut else { return }  // a LUT has no thumbnails, peaks or speech
191	        DecoderSupport.enable()
192	        let input = ThumbnailInput(media: media, urls: urls)  // spec §11 GR-21
193	        CacheLedger.shared.enqueue(
194	            cacheDir: cacheDir, media: media.id, url: url, input: input?.color  // = convertingColor(of:)
195	        ) { previous, bounded, pass in
196	            Task.detached(priority: .utility) {
197	                await awaitPass(previous, bounded: bounded)
198	                guard pass.isCurrent() else {
199	                    pass.done()
200	                    return
201	                }
202	                // After the await: the stamp is of the file as THIS pass
203	                // finds it, not as it was when the pass was asked for.
204	                let stamp = CacheStamp.stamp(for: media, url: url)
205	                await thumbnails(
206	                    for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass, input: input)
207	                let published = await peaks(
208	                    for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
209	                let loudnessPublished = await loudness(
210	                    for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
211	                await syncFeatures(for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
212	                await speech(for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
213	                if !(published && loudnessPublished), pass.isCurrent() {
214	                    await retryPeaks(for: media, url: url, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
215	                }
216	                pass.done()
217	            }
218	        }
219	    }
220	
221	    /// `body` on `CacheLane.shared`, awaited (spec §11 #367).
222	    static func onCacheLane<T>(_ body: @escaping () -> T) async -> T {
223	        await withCheckedContinuation { cont in CacheLane.shared.submit { cont.resume(returning: body()) } }
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The waits between a failed waveform pass and its in-session retries.
227	    static let peaksRetryDelays: [Duration] = [.seconds(2), .seconds(10)]
228	
229	    /// Waits for the pass enqueued before this one. Unbounded, it is the
230	    /// same-file order. Bounded — the previous pass was superseded and
231	    /// cancelled — it returns when that pass ends or `CacheLedger.waitLimit`
232	    /// passes, whichever is first: a checked continuation resumed once by
233	    /// whichever of two detached tasks gets there first. Not a task group or
234	    /// `async let`, which would wait for the child still awaiting the stuck
235	    /// task, and `Task.value` ignores cancellation. The sleeper is cancelled
236	    /// once the wait returns, and returned (nil when nothing slept) for a probe.
237	    @discardableResult
238	    static func awaitPass(
239	        _ previous: Task<Void, Never>?, bounded: Bool
240	    ) async -> Task<Void, Never>? {
241	        guard let previous else { return nil }
242	        guard bounded else {
243	            await previous.value
244	            return nil
245	        }
246	        var sleeper: Task<Void, Never>?
247	        await withCheckedContinuation { (continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, Never>) in
248	            let once = ResumeOnce(continuation)
249	            Task.detached {
250	                await previous.value
251	                once.resume()
252	            }
253	            sleeper = Task.detached {
254	                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(CacheLedger.waitLimit))
255	                once.resume()
256	            }
257	        }
258	        sleeper?.cancel()
259	        return sleeper
260	    }
261	
262	    /// The in-session retry of a waveform or loudness pass that published nothing: after each
263	    /// delay (a cancellation ends the wait), while the pass is current, with a fresh stamp. An
264	    /// attempt whose `peaks` lands runs `loudness`, `syncFeatures` and `speech` with that stamp
265	    /// (SY-11, SY-17) and ends the retry when the loudness file landed too (spec §11 AU-10).
266	    private static func retryPeaks(
267	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, into cacheDir: URL, pass: CachePass
268	    ) async {
269	        for delay in peaksRetryDelays {
270	            do { try await Task.sleep(for: delay) } catch { return }
271	            guard pass.isCurrent() else { return }
272	            let stamp = CacheStamp.stamp(for: media, url: url)
273	            if await peaks(for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass) {
274	                let landed = await loudness(
275	                    for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
276	                // SY-11, SY-17: features and speech lost with the waveform land with it.
277	                await syncFeatures(for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
278	                await speech(for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
279	                if landed { return }
280	            }
281	        }
282	    }

284	    // MARK: - Thumbnails
285	
286	    /// Writes the filmstrip for `media`: 160 px tall JPEGs, one per second up
287	    /// to `maxThumbnails`, into `cache/thumbs/<id>/<index>.jpg`. Posts
288	    /// `.mediaCacheDidChange` as batches land so the timeline fills in while
289	    /// the rest is still decoding.
290	    ///
291	    /// Tolerance is deliberately half a second in both directions: a
292	    /// filmstrip wants the nearest keyframe, not an exact frame, and zero
293	    /// tolerance here makes a long clip take minutes instead of seconds.
294	    ///
295	    /// **A second at or past the VIDEO track's last frame asks for that
296	    /// frame** (road map 3's R0 surprise). A screen recording's picture ends
297	    /// at the last screen change while its sound runs on, and the record's
298	    /// `duration` is the asset's — the sound's — so every second past the
299	    /// picture's end FAILED (`AVFoundationErrorDomain -11832`) and left a
300	    /// tinted hole under a marker that certified it: a narrated still screen
301	    /// read as a strip of holes. The cure is at the REQUEST, not in the
302	    /// failure arm: the last frame's own time is read off the TRACK
303	    /// (`lastFrameTime`, in the one file that may `await`), the held seconds
304	    /// ask for it ONCE, and the one decode is written under each of them — a
305	    /// static ten-minute recording costs one tail decode, not six hundred —
306	    /// and the strip is TRUE, since `CompositionBuilder.fill` holds that same
307	    /// frame over the same tail. It is the TRACK's frame and never the
308	    /// record's: a sparse recording's `nominalFrameRate` is its frame count
309	    /// over its length — three frames in 50 s read as 0.06 fps, a 16.7 s
310	    /// "frame" — so a tail measured from the record's rate held the slide
311	    /// BEFORE the last one from 34 s on while the composition showed the
312	    /// last. Copying the last landed tile under a FAILED request instead
313	    /// would have drawn a freeze wherever a frame inside the picture will not
314	    /// decode; a failure still leaves a hole. A file with no video track, or
315	    /// none AVFoundation can open, has no end to read and runs as it always
316	    /// did. The every-16 post counts TILES, so a held tail posts as its
317	    /// seconds land and an ordinary strip posts as it did.
318	    ///
319	    /// What the generator answers between frames, measured: see `thumbnailRequests`.
320	    ///
321	    /// Skipped outright when `thumbs/<id>/complete.json` holds `stamp` — the
322	    /// file's `CacheStamp` as `generateCaches` measured it: no decode, no
323	    /// post. Otherwise whatever is on disk is cleared first and the marker
324	    /// is written after the loop, so the marker means "a pass over this file
325	    /// finished, and what it wrote is here" and nothing weaker.
326	    static func thumbnails(
327	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, stamp: CacheStamp?, into cacheDir: URL,
328	        pass: CachePass? = nil, input: ThumbnailInput? = nil
329	    ) async {
330	        guard media.hasVideo else { return }
331	        // A still's label, resolved before the head check (spec §11 HD-21).
332	        let input = media.kind == .image ? input ?? ThumbnailInput(still: url) : input
333	        let directory = thumbsDirectory(for: media.id, in: cacheDir)
334	        let marker = thumbsMarkerURL(for: media.id, in: cacheDir)
335	        // The head check. A nil stamp (the file cannot be stat'ed) never
336	        // skips, and never writes a marker below either.
337	        if let stamp, thumbsAreCurrent(stamp, input: input, url: url, at: marker) { return }
338	        guard pass?.isCurrent() ?? true, ensureDirectory(directory) else { return }
339	        // What is on disk is the old film or a partial pass. The marker goes
340	        // first, then the frames (`clearThumbnails` says why in that order).
341	        // `replaced` rides the FIRST post of this pass and no other. The
342	        // timeline memoises decoded tiles, so the old film's are in its memo
343	        // and the first post must drop them; the first also suffices,
344	        // because nothing of the old film is on disk once `clearThumbnails`
345	        // returns — every tile memoised after that post is this pass's, and
346	        // a miss is cleared by every post anyway. On every post it would
347	        // empty the whole media's memo every sixteen frames for nothing.
348	        var replaced = clearThumbnails(in: directory)
349	        // The indices `writeJPEG` succeeded on: what the marker vouches for.
350	        var written: Set<Int> = []
351	
352	        if media.kind == .image {
353	            // An HLG or PQ still's tile through step 0 (spec §11 HD-21).
354	            let reader = input.flatMap { stillReader(for: media, url: url, input: $0) }
355	            var drawn: CGImage?
356	            if let reader {
357	                drawn = try? await reader.generator.image(at: .zero).image
358	                reader.finish()
359	            }
360	            writeImageThumbnail(
361	                for: media, url: url, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass,
362	                directory: directory, marker: marker, replaced: replaced, input: input,
363	                drawn: drawn)
364	            return
365	        }
366	
367	        let seconds = thumbnailSeconds(for: media)
368	        // Precise timing, so a sample cursor lands on the exact sample
369	        // (`AVAssetTrack.h`); the generator parses the table anyway.
370	        let asset = AVURLAsset(
371	            url: url, options: [AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey: true])
372	        // The held request: the last frame's own time on the track, or — no
373	        // track, or none the file can open — one record frame before the
374	        // record's end, which is where an ordinary strip always ended.
375	        var lastTime = CompositionBuilder.time(
376	            max(0, media.duration - max(1, media.fps.frameDuration)))
377	        let track = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .video))?.first
378	        if let track, let frame = await lastFrameTime(of: track) { lastTime = frame }
379	        let (held, times) = thumbnailRequests(seconds: seconds, lastTime: lastTime)
380	
381	        let reader = thumbnailReader(for: media, asset: asset, track: track, input: input)
382	        defer { reader.finish() }
383	        let generator = reader.generator
384	
385	        var sinceLastPost = 0
386	        frames: for await result in generator.images(for: times) {
387	            var tiles = 1
388	            switch result {
389	            case .success(requestedTime: let requested, image: let image, actualTime: _):
390	                guard let count = writeTiles(
391	                    image, requested: requested, lastTime: lastTime, held: held,
392	                    directory: directory, pass: pass, into: &written)
393	                else { break frames }
394	                tiles = count
395	            case .failure:
396	                // A frame that will not decode leaves a hole in the strip;
397	                // the timeline draws the clip's tint there and carries on.
398	                break
399	            @unknown default:
400	                break
401	            }
402	            sinceLastPost += tiles
403	            if sinceLastPost >= 16 {
404	                sinceLastPost = 0
405	                postCacheChange(media: media.id, kind: thumbsKind, replaced: replaced)
406	                replaced = false
407	            }
408	        }
409	        publishThumbnails(
410	            written, reader: reader, for: media, stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass,
411	            directory: directory, marker: marker, replaced: replaced)
412	    }
413	
414	    /// The presentation time of `track`'s last frame on the track's own
415	    /// timeline — what the held seconds ask the generator for. A sample
416	    /// cursor at the end of the sample table (a table read, no decode), whose
417	    /// time is the MEDIA's and is mapped through the edit that places it: an
418	    /// x264 file with B-frames starts its media 1/30 s in, and `-vsync vfr`
419	    /// put a 50 s media offset on a three-frame file. A mapping at any other
420	    /// rate, or a file that offers no cursor, falls back to one
421	    /// `minFrameDuration` before the track's end — the composition's own
422	    /// window, exact wherever the end is; nil for a track with no numeric
423	    /// extent, which then runs on the record's arithmetic.
424	    private static func lastFrameTime(of track: AVAssetTrack) async -> CMTime? {
425	        guard let range = try? await track.load(.timeRange), range.end.isNumeric else { return nil }
426	        if (try? await track.load(.canProvideSampleCursors)) == true,
427	            let mapping = (try? await track.load(.segments))?.last(where: { !$0.isEmpty })?
428	                .timeMapping,
429	            mapping.source.duration == mapping.target.duration,
430	            let cursor = track.makeSampleCursor(presentationTimeStamp: mapping.source.end),
431	            cursor.presentationTimeStamp.isNumeric {
432	            return mapping.target.start + (cursor.presentationTimeStamp - mapping.source.start)
433	        }
434	        let frame = (try? await track.load(.minFrameDuration)) ?? .invalid
435	        let step = frame.isNumeric && frame > .zero ? frame : CompositionBuilder.time(1)
436	        return CMTimeMaximum(.zero, range.end - step)
437	    }

439	    // MARK: - Peaks
440	
441	    /// Writes the waveform for `media` to `cache/peaks/<id>.bin`: the
442	    /// reader's every sample buffer through `PeakBuckets`
443	    /// (`MediaPeakBuckets.swift`), then one atomic write of its floats after
444	    /// successful whole-track coverage.
445	    ///
446	    /// Skipped when `peaks/<id>.complete.json` holds `PeaksStamp(stamp)` AND
447	    /// its `.bin` is valid — the marker is a sibling, not a child, so either can be
448	    /// deleted without the other. Otherwise BOTH go, before anything below
449	    /// can fail, and a removed `.bin` is posted at once (`clearPeaks` says
450	    /// why: readers may memoize a waveform, so a withdrawal must invalidate
451	    /// it). No track, unusable extent, reader failure or incomplete decode
452	    /// writes no marker or `.bin`; `generateCaches` retries it in the same
453	    /// session (`retryPeaks`). Answers true when there is nothing to make or
454	    /// the waveform is current or published, false otherwise — a superseded
455	    /// pass included. A media with no audio (a relink to a silent file, #180)
456	    /// withdraws and posts a `.bin` still on disk the same way, while current.
457	    @discardableResult
458	    static func peaks(
459	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, stamp: CacheStamp?, into cacheDir: URL,
460	        pass: CachePass? = nil
461	    ) async -> Bool {
462	        guard media.hasAudio, media.duration > 0 else {
463	            if pass?.isCurrent() ?? true, clearPeaks(for: media.id, in: cacheDir) {
464	                postCacheChange(media: media.id, kind: peaksKind)
465	            }
466	            return true
467	        }
468	        if peaksAreCurrent(for: media, stamp: stamp, in: cacheDir) { return true }
469	        guard pass?.isCurrent() ?? true else { return false }
470	        if clearPeaks(for: media.id, in: cacheDir) {
471	            postCacheChange(media: media.id, kind: peaksKind)
472	        }
473	        let asset = AVURLAsset(url: url)
474	        guard let track = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio))?.first else {
475	            return false
476	        }
477	        guard let trackRange = try? await track.load(.timeRange),
478	            let segments = try? await track.load(.segments),
479	            let expected = expectedPeaksRanges(trackRange: trackRange, segments: segments)
480	        else { return false }

482	            writePeaks(for: media, asset: asset, track: track, expectedRanges: expected,
483	                       stamp: stamp, into: cacheDir, pass: pass)

524	    ) async {

526	            if pass?.isCurrent() ?? true { clearSyncFeatures(for: media.id, in: cacheDir) }

528	        }
529	        guard !syncFeaturesAreCurrent(for: media, stamp: stamp, in: cacheDir) else { return }

544	    /// Writes `cache/speech/<id>.bin` — road map 4's voice cache, run AFTER
545	    /// `peaks` in `generateCaches`'s order (never before it), so the `.bin`
546	    /// withdrawal at `peaks`' own head is never held behind a full-file
547	    /// decode and an inference pass.
548	    ///
549	    /// Skipped when `speechIsCurrent` (`MediaImporter+Speech.swift`'s head
550	    /// check) says the marker, the model and the chunk size all still agree,
551	    /// or when there is no audio at all, which while current withdraws and
552	    /// posts a `.bin` left on disk as below (#180). A stale cache is cleared
553	    /// and posted at once — `clearSpeech`'s doc argues the order — and that
554	    /// withdrawal is the first post of a pass replacing a `.bin` on disk, so
555	    /// it carries `replaced` (§4g claim 14), the one way it differs from
556	    /// `peaks`'. Then `SileroVAD.isAvailable` is asked exactly once: a model
557	    /// already marked unavailable this process (a nil bundle, an earlier
558	    /// thrown prediction) is not retried, so a project full of media pays for
559	    /// it once, not per file.
560	    static func speech(
561	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, stamp: CacheStamp?, into cacheDir: URL,
562	        pass: CachePass? = nil
563	    ) async {
564	        guard media.hasAudio, media.duration > 0 else {
565	            if pass?.isCurrent() ?? true, clearSpeech(for: media.id, in: cacheDir) {
566	                postCacheChange(media: media.id, kind: speechKind, replaced: true)
567	            }
568	            return
569	        }
570	        guard !speechIsCurrent(for: media, stamp: stamp, in: cacheDir) else { return }
571	        guard pass?.isCurrent() ?? true else { return }
572	        if clearSpeech(for: media.id, in: cacheDir) {
573	            postCacheChange(media: media.id, kind: speechKind, replaced: true)
574	        }
575	        guard SileroVAD.isAvailable else { return }
576	        let asset = AVURLAsset(url: url)
577	        guard let track = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio))?.first else {
578	            return
579	        }
580	        await onCacheLane {
581	            writeSpeech(for: media, asset: asset, track: track, stamp: stamp,
582	                        into: cacheDir, pass: pass)
583	        }
584	    }
585	}

6	/// The await-free half of `MediaImporter`: the refusal type, the still-image
7	/// question, the ImageIO probe of a still, and the rate table
8	/// `rationalFrameRate` rounds a track's float onto. It also holds the
9	/// probe's synchronous faces (`probe(url:mayAsk:completion:)`,
10	/// `probeAllowingRewrap`, `probeBlocking`, with `withoutAsking`), which wait through `waitForProbe`. Nothing here touches
11	/// AVFoundation's loading API — every `await` is in `MediaImporter.swift`,
12	/// the one file that may (app/CLAUDE.md) — and every member keeps its
13	/// `MediaImporter.` spelling at every call site, so the cut is invisible from
14	/// outside: it exists because road map 3's held tail took the base file over
15	/// the ~600-line cap, and the members that owe nothing to the seam are the
16	/// ones that could leave. `MediaCacheFiles.swift` is the same shape for the
17	/// cache half.
18	extension MediaImporter {
19	
20	    // MARK: - Errors
21	
22	    /// Import refusals. Every one is shown in an alert and never crashes;
23	    /// `unreadable` is also what a relink of a moved file reports.
24	    enum ImportError: LocalizedError {
25	        case unreadable(URL)
26	        case noTracks(URL)
27	        case timedOut(URL)
28	        /// The video track's first frame will not decode here (spec §11
29	        /// #216); the sentence names the codec (`DecoderSupport.refusal`).
30	        case undecodable(URL, sentence: String)
31	
32	        var errorDescription: String? {
33	            switch self {
34	            case .unreadable(let url):
35	                return "Could not read \(url.lastPathComponent)."
36	            case .noTracks(let url):
37	                return "\(url.lastPathComponent) has no video or audio the app can open."
38	            case .timedOut(let url):
39	                return "Timed out reading \(url.lastPathComponent)."
40	            case .undecodable(_, let sentence):
41	                return sentence
42	            }
43	        }
44	
45	        /// Whether a user-installed ffmpeg is worth offering (`FFmpegRewrap`).
46	        ///
47	        /// `unreadable` is the one that matters: AVFoundation answers a
48	        /// Matroska or a WebM with `AVFoundationErrorDomain -11828 "Cannot
49	        /// Open"` on the *container*, before it has looked at the codecs
50	        /// inside, so a plain H.264 recording in an `.mkv` lands here and is
51	        /// one stream copy away from importing. `noTracks` is included
52	        /// because a container AVFoundation half-understands can report a
53	        /// duration and no tracks; `FFmpegRewrap.plan` refuses a file that
54	        /// genuinely has no video and no audio, so a truly empty one keeps
55	        /// this message. `timedOut` is not: a stalled network mount will
56	        /// stall ffmpeg too, and the second wait is not a kindness. Nor is
57	        /// `undecodable`: the refusal is final (spec §11 #216).
58	        var invitesFFmpeg: Bool {
59	            switch self {
60	            case .unreadable, .noTracks: return true
61	            case .timedOut, .undecodable: return false
62	            }
63	        }
64	    }
65	
66	    // MARK: - Stills
67	
68	    /// Still-image types ImageIO decodes and AVFoundation would refuse.
69	    /// Probed with ImageIO and imported as `kind: image` (§7.7).
70	    static let imageTypes: [UTType] = [.png, .jpeg, .heic, .heif, .tiff, .gif, .bmp, .webP]
71	
72	    /// Whether `url` is a still picture rather than a movie. Type-based, not
73	    /// extension-based, so a `.heic` written by a camera and a `.jpeg` with
74	    /// no extension both land in the same branch.
75	    static func isImage(_ url: URL) -> Bool {
76	        guard let type = UTType(filenameExtension: url.pathExtension.lowercased()) else {
77	            return false
78	        }
79	        return imageTypes.contains { type.conforms(to: $0) }
80	    }
81	
82	    /// ImageIO's view of a still: pixel size, and alpha from the file's own
83	    /// properties. Duration 0 — an `image` clip has no source bound and any
84	    /// duration (§5.2).
85	    static func probeImage(_ url: URL) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
86	        guard let source = CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url as CFURL, nil),
87	            CGImageSourceGetCount(source) > 0,
88	            let props = CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex(source, 0, nil) as? [CFString: Any]
89	        else {
90	            throw ImportError.unreadable(url)
91	        }
92	        let width = (props[kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth] as? Int) ?? 0
93	        let height = (props[kCGImagePropertyPixelHeight] as? Int) ?? 0
94	        guard width > 0, height > 0 else { throw ImportError.unreadable(url) }
95	        let hasAlpha = (props[kCGImagePropertyHasAlpha] as? Bool) ?? false
96	        // `hasVideo` is true for a still: it contributes pixels, so
97	        // `enabled.video` means something on its clips. It still gets NO
98	        // composition track — the recipe names an image layer `image`, not
99	        // `track` (§7.2), and the plan never lists it.
100	        var descriptor = MediaDescriptor(
101	            path: url.path, bookmark: bookmarkString(for: url), kind: .image, duration: 0,
102	            width: width, height: height, fps: .thirty, hasVideo: true, hasAudio: false,
103	            hasAlpha: hasAlpha)
104	        // A PQ still's peak, as a PQ video's (spec §11 HD-20 (b)).
105	        descriptor.color = detectedStillPQ(url)
106	        return descriptor
107	    }
108	
109	    // MARK: - Rates
110	
111	    /// The rates a container is allowed to round: the integer rates and the
112	    /// three NTSC /1001 rates (§7.7). Anything else keeps three decimals as
113	    /// `[round(fps × 1000), 1000]`, which is exact enough to place source
114	    /// frames and never pretends a 47.3 fps screen recording is 48.
115	    static let commonRates: [Fps] = [
116	        Fps(num: 24, den: 1), Fps(num: 24000, den: 1001), Fps(num: 25, den: 1),
117	        Fps(num: 30, den: 1), Fps(num: 30000, den: 1001), Fps(num: 48, den: 1),
118	        Fps(num: 50, den: 1), Fps(num: 60, den: 1), Fps(num: 60000, den: 1001),
119	    ]
120	
121	    /// Tolerance for that match, in frames per second. 0.01 is wide enough
122	    /// for a float's error at 60 fps and narrower than the 0.03 gap between
123	    /// 29.97 and 30 — the pair this must never confuse.
124	    static let rateTolerance = 0.01
125	
126	    static func rationalFrameRate(_ nominal: Double) -> Fps {
127	        guard nominal.isFinite, nominal > 0 else { return .thirty }
128	        for candidate in commonRates where abs(candidate.double - nominal) <= rateTolerance {
129	            return candidate
130	        }
131	        return Fps(num: Int((nominal * 1000).rounded()), den: 1000)
132	    }
133	
134	    // MARK: - The synchronous faces
135	
136	    /// The longest `waitForProbe` waits for one AVFoundation probe.
137	    static let probeTimeout: TimeInterval = 30
138	
139	    /// The queue the completion-handler face probes on. A serial queue, not
140	    /// the cooperative pool: a conversion (`FFmpegRewrap`) blocks its thread
141	    /// for as long as ffmpeg runs, which is exactly what a cooperative
142	    /// thread must never do, and serialising means a batch drop of four
143	    /// unreadable files asks four questions in order rather than stacking
144	    /// four alerts. `app/CLAUDE.md` names import as one of the documented
145	    /// `DispatchQueue` seams.
146	    private static let importQueue = DispatchQueue(
147	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.import", qos: .userInitiated)
148	
149	    /// The synchronous face of `probe` for the rest of the app: the result
150	    /// arrives on the main thread, so the caller can go straight to
151	    /// `add_media` + `add_clip` without ever writing `await`. `mayAsk` is
152	    /// the caller's: true for a person's click, false for a tool call's.
153	    /// `watch` is too: a click door's sees a WebM or Matroska copy start
154	    /// (spec §11 #228-P), and a tool call passes none.
155	    static func probe(
156	        url: URL, mayAsk: Bool, watch: RewrapWatch? = nil,
157	        completion: @escaping (Result<MediaDescriptor, any Error>) -> Void
158	    ) {
159	        importQueue.async {
160	            let outcome = Result { try probeAllowingRewrap(url, mayAsk: mayAsk, watch: watch) }
161	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(outcome) }
162	        }
163	    }
164	
165	    /// The AVFoundation probe plus spec §11's opt-in ffmpeg step, and the
166	    /// body of both synchronous faces.
167	    ///
168	    /// The two halves are deliberately not nested inside `probe(url:)`.
169	    /// `waitForProbe` puts a 30-second ceiling (`probeTimeout`) on
170	    /// AVFoundation, which is right for reading headers and catastrophically
171	    /// wrong for a transcode; `FFmpegRewrap.assist` therefore runs OUTSIDE
172	    /// it, under its own bounds (`FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist`), and its
173	    /// result is probed with a fresh ceiling of its own. `assist` also needs
174	    /// the main thread for its consent alert, which it can only have because
175	    /// this function's callers are never the thread being waited on.
176	    ///
177	    /// Every one of the four import paths funnels through here — document
178	    /// open (`ProjectDocument.readMediaFile`), File ▸ Add Media… and Finder
179	    /// drops (`ProjectDocument.probeNext`), and the agent's `import_media`
180	    /// (`AgentServer+Media.probe`) — so an MKV opens the same way in all of
181	    /// them, and `assist` answering `nil` leaves all four with exactly the
182	    /// failure they report on a machine that has no ffmpeg. The built-in
183	    /// copy records the file it was made from as the descriptor's
184	    /// `original` (spec §11 #228-O), on every door alike, and so does an
185	    /// ffmpeg conversion (#233).
186	    ///
187	    /// **Who may be asked is decided by the caller** (spec §11 MC-5), never
188	    /// read from process-wide state: each place a tool call hands work to the
189	    /// importer passes `mayAsk: false` (`import_media`, `relink_media`,
190	    /// `record_screen`) or wraps its open in `withoutAsking` (`open_project`),
191	    /// and every click path passes `true`, so a person's own import still
192	    /// asks while a tool call runs.
193	    ///
194	    /// **Known cost of the document-open path.** NSDocumentController reads
195	    /// a person's File ▸ Open or Finder double-click on its concurrent read
196	    /// queue (`canConcurrentlyReadDocuments`), so the main thread is free
197	    /// for the built-in copy's progress window, which `watch` feeds and
198	    /// whose Cancel stops the copy (spec §11 #228-P; `probeForOpening`
199	    /// passes it there). An agent's `open_project` reads on the lane's
200	    /// thread inside `withoutAsking` (spec §11 #231), where no watch is
201	    /// passed: main is free, and the call waits the copy's length with no
202	    /// window. A read AppKit itself runs ON main passes no watch either, and
203	    /// there a copy — or an ffmpeg conversion, on any door, which reports no
204	    /// progress — blocks the window for its length; ffmpeg's consent alert
205	    /// states the cost first.
206	    private static func probeAllowingRewrap(
207	        _ url: URL, mayAsk: Bool, watch: RewrapWatch?
208	    ) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
209	        do {
210	            return withCursorBeside(try waitForProbe(url), movie: url)  // spec §11 CU-34 (a)
211	        } catch let failure as ImportError where failure.invitesFFmpeg && !isImage(url) {
212	            // Images are excluded because ImageIO's refusal means the picture
213	            // is corrupt, not that the container is exotic — and a PNG is not
214	            // something to hand to a video converter.
215	            guard ContainerRewrap.isMatroska(url) else {
216	                return try probeConverted(url, failure: failure, mayAsk: mayAsk)
217	            }
218	            // A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a movie with no question
219	            // (spec §11 #216-R). Only a codec the copy cannot carry goes on
220	            // to the opt-in ffmpeg step; every other refusal is final.
221	            do {
222	                return try probeCopy(try ContainerRewrap.assist(url, watch: watch), of: url)
223	            } catch let refusal as ContainerRewrapError where refusal.invitesFFmpeg {
224	                return try probeConverted(url, failure: refusal, mayAsk: mayAsk)
225	            }
226	        }
227	    }
228	
229	    /// The opt-in ffmpeg step, and its result probed, with `url` recorded as
230	    /// its `original` (spec §11 #233); `failure` is what is thrown when there
231	    /// is no conversion or it will not open. `mayAsk` is the caller's (spec
232	    /// §11 MC-5): a tool call's is false, so it never raises the consent
233	    /// question.
234	    ///
235	    /// There is ONE second attempt (spec §11 #227): when ffmpeg failed, a
236	    /// VP9 copy failed its frame check, or the file will not open, the step
237	    /// is asked again to re-encode a VP9 stream it had copied, with the
238	    /// first attempt's plan. A source whose plan copied no VP9 gets no
239	    /// second call, and then the first attempt's error is the one thrown. A
240	    /// timeout is not tried again.
241	    private static func probeConverted(
242	        _ url: URL, failure: any Error, mayAsk: Bool
243	    ) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
244	        var remembered = failure
245	        var converted: URL?
246	        var failed = false
247	        var planned: FFmpegRewrap.Plan?
248	        do {
249	            converted = try FFmpegRewrap.assist(url, mayAsk: mayAsk, planned: &planned)
250	        } catch let refusal as FFmpegRewrap.RewrapError {
251	            guard case .failed = refusal else { throw refusal }
252	            (remembered, failed) = (refusal, true)
253	        }
254	        if let converted {
255	            if let descriptor = probeConversion(converted, of: url) { return descriptor }
256	        } else if !failed {
257	            throw failure
258	        }
259	        if let planned, !planned.copiesVP9 { throw remembered }
260	        guard
261	            let again = try FFmpegRewrap.assist(
262	                url, mayAsk: mayAsk, planned: &planned, reencodingVP9: true)
263	        else { throw remembered }
264	        guard let descriptor = probeConversion(again, of: url) else { throw failure }
265	        return descriptor
266	    }
267	
268	    /// A conversion of `url` probed, with `url` as its `original`; nil, and
269	    /// the file thrown away, when AVFoundation still will not open it. The
270	    /// conversion is cached by name, so leaving it there would hand the same
271	    /// broken result back for ever; throwing it away makes the next attempt
272	    /// a real attempt. Only the file that was probed is thrown away: one
273	    /// another import has since put at the name is left (spec §11 #227). The
274	    /// error its caller reports is the ORIGINAL one, because the file the
275	    /// user chose is the one they are being told about.
276	    private static func probeConversion(_ rewrapped: URL, of url: URL) -> MediaDescriptor? {
277	        let probed = FFmpegRewrap.fileNumber(of: rewrapped)
278	        guard var descriptor = try? waitForProbe(rewrapped) else {
279	            FFmpegRewrap.discard(rewrapped, ifStill: probed)
280	            return nil
281	        }
282	        descriptor.original = MediaOriginal(of: url)
283	        return descriptor
284	    }
285	
286	    /// The built-in copy of `source` probed, with `source` recorded as its
287	    /// `original` (spec §11 #228-O). A copy the one-frame decode
288	    /// refuses is thrown away and refused in the source's name (#216's
289	    /// backstop); any other failure throws the copy away too, so the next
290	    /// import copies again rather than reuse a movie that will not open.
291	    private static func probeCopy(_ copy: URL, of source: URL) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
292	        do {
293	            var descriptor = try waitForProbe(copy)
294	            descriptor.original = MediaOriginal(of: source)
295	            return descriptor
296	        } catch ImportError.undecodable(_, let sentence) {
297	            FFmpegRewrap.discard(copy)
298	            let copyName = copy.lastPathComponent
299	            let named = sentence.hasPrefix(copyName)
300	                ? source.lastPathComponent + sentence.dropFirst(copyName.count) : sentence
301	            throw ImportError.undecodable(source, sentence: named)
302	        } catch {
303	            FFmpegRewrap.discard(copy)
304	            throw ContainerRewrapError.failed(source, reason: "the copied movie could not be read")
305	        }
306	    }
307	
308	    /// The built-in copy of `source`, probed: the open-time re-copy of a
309	    /// copy that is gone (`ProjectDocument.recopyingMissingCopies`, spec §11
310	    /// #228-O). Never ffmpeg and never a question; `watch` as `assist`'s.
311	    static func probeBuiltInCopy(of source: URL, watch: RewrapWatch?) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
312	        try probeCopy(try ContainerRewrap.assist(source, watch: watch), of: source)
313	    }
314	
315	    /// The BLOCKING face of `probe`, for `ProjectDocument.read(from:ofType:)`.
316	    ///
317	    /// That method is synchronous by contract and CAN run on the main thread
318	    /// — NSDocumentController's open path does not always take the concurrent
319	    /// read queue (an agent's `open_project` reads on the lane's thread,
320	    /// spec §11 #231). So this must never wait on the main actor. The obvious
321	    /// spelling (a completion delivered through `MainActor.run`, joined with
322	    /// a `DispatchGroup`) deadlocks exactly there: the waiter is holding the
323	    /// one thread the completion needs, and the open dies on the timeout
324	    /// instead of the file. Here the work runs on the cooperative pool and
325	    /// the result comes back through a plain semaphore, so the waiting thread
326	    /// is never the thread being waited on. It may ask, and pass `watch`,
327	    /// unless this thread is inside `withoutAsking`.
328	    static func probeBlocking(url: URL, watch: RewrapWatch? = nil) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
329	        let quiet = isWithoutAsking
330	        return try probeAllowingRewrap(url, mayAsk: !quiet, watch: quiet ? nil : watch)
331	    }
332	
333	    /// Whether this thread is inside `withoutAsking`.
334	    static var isWithoutAsking: Bool {
335	        Thread.current.threadDictionary[withoutAskingKey] as? Bool ?? false
336	    }
337	
338	    private static let withoutAskingKey = "com.kgalligan.framejob.import.withoutAsking"
339	
340	    /// Runs `body` with `probeBlocking` on THIS thread never asking and
341	    /// never passing a watch — the scope a tool call's synchronous document
342	    /// open runs in, on the lane's thread (spec §11 MC-5, #231); the re-copy
343	    /// on open reads it too (`isWithoutAsking`). The prior value is put back
344	    /// on every exit.
345	    static func withoutAsking<T>(_ body: () throws -> T) rethrows -> T {
346	        let dictionary = Thread.current.threadDictionary
347	        let prior = dictionary[withoutAskingKey]
348	        dictionary[withoutAskingKey] = true
349	        defer { dictionary[withoutAskingKey] = prior }
350	        return try body()
351	    }
352	
353	    /// Carries one probe's outcome across the semaphore in `waitForProbe`.
354	    /// Unchecked because the join is the synchronisation: the detached task
355	    /// writes it, signals, and never touches it again; the waiter reads it
356	    /// only after the wait returns.
357	    final class ProbeBox: @unchecked Sendable {
358	        var outcome: Result<MediaDescriptor, any Error>?
359	    }
360	
361	    /// Whether the codec carries alpha. The format description's own flag
362	    /// first (ProRes 4444 and animation-with-alpha set it); the codec type is
363	    /// the fallback for files whose writer omitted the extension.
364	    static func hasAlphaChannel(_ descriptions: [CMFormatDescription]) -> Bool {
365	        for description in descriptions {
366	            if let flag = CMFormatDescriptionGetExtension(
367	                description, extensionKey: kCMFormatDescriptionExtension_ContainsAlphaChannel)
368	                as? Bool, flag {
369	                return true
370	            }
371	            switch CMFormatDescriptionGetMediaSubType(description) {
